source_of_truth: The frozen judge-only reference dossier; candidates answer from internal knowledge.
evaluation_principles: Separate diagnostic accuracy from evidence that a screening program improves outcomes.
Reward clear distinctions among false positives, overdiagnosis and screening biases.

key_facts.label: Correct 10,000-person table
key_facts.expected: Calculates 100 diseased, 90 true positives, 10 false negatives, 9,900 non-diseased, 495 false positives and 9,405 true negatives.

key_facts.label: Positive predictive value
key_facts.expected: Calculates 90 true positives among 585 positives, or about 15.4% PPV.

key_facts.label: Base-rate explanation
key_facts.expected: Explains why prevalence changes predictive value even when sensitivity and specificity are fixed.

key_facts.label: Result is not diagnosis
key_facts.expected: Treats the positive screen as updated evidence requiring clinical interpretation or confirmation, not a diagnosis.

key_facts.label: False-result harms
key_facts.expected: Covers harms of both false positives and false negatives.

key_facts.label: Lead-time and length bias
key_facts.expected: Correctly distinguishes earlier diagnostic timing from longer life and preferential detection of slower disease.

key_facts.label: Overdiagnosis and overtreatment
key_facts.expected: Defines overdiagnosis as a real condition that would not become clinically consequential and links it to possible overtreatment.

key_facts.label: Better endpoints and design
key_facts.expected: Prefers randomized comparisons of mortality, morbidity, quality of life and harms with sufficient follow-up.

key_ideas.label: Conditional probabilities differ
key_ideas.expected: Makes clear that P(positive given disease) is not P(disease given positive).

key_ideas.label: Screening is a pathway
key_ideas.expected: Evaluates population, test, follow-up, treatment, benefits and harms as one pathway.

key_ideas.label: Detection metrics can mislead
key_ideas.expected: Explains why case counts and post-diagnosis survival can improve without extending lives.

key_ideas.label: Evidence limits decision
key_ideas.expected: Does not infer a personal or policy recommendation from the hypothetical calculation alone.

known_critical_errors.description: States that the positive predictive value is 90% or 95%.
Produces a materially wrong natural-frequency table or PPV.
Defines overdiagnosis as a false-positive test.
Claims that longer survival measured from diagnosis proves longer life.
Gives an individual diagnosis or treatment recommendation from the hypothetical screen.

nonessential_details: Named diseases not specified in the scenario

anchors.25: Calculation and screening concepts are accurate.
anchors.20: Accurate overall with one minor imprecision.
anchors.12: At least one major error or several meaningful imprecisions.

anchors.10: Connects the numbers, base rate and outcome biases coherently.
anchors.7: Sound explanation with one underdeveloped connection.
anchors.4: Mostly lists concepts without integrating them.

anchors.10: Carefully separates screening evidence, diagnosis and program benefit.
anchors.7: Mostly calibrated with one limited overstatement.
anchors.4: Repeatedly overstates what the scenario proves.

anchors.10: Clear German, helpful headings and intelligible without specialist training.

anchors.5: High information density without material repetition.
anchors.0: Exceeds the hard maximum or is not focused.
